Dear guests, taste our new hot dish!

And I really want more of this food!
I literally cannot stop, it is so tasty!

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.text: Купидон решает судьбы всех влюблённых людей.
examples.trans: Cupid decides the fates of all people in love.

examples.text: Прекрати сейчас же всю эту нежную ерунду!
examples.trans: Stop all this mushy nonsense right now!

examples.text: Пусть всё это останется строго конфиденциально.
examples.trans: Let all this remain strictly confidential.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'clear'.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'definitely'.

examples.text: Всё понятно, это точно сильный стимулятор!
examples.trans: Everything is clear, this is definitely a strong stimulant!

examples.text: Лёля точно придёт!

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'strong', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Всё понятно, это точно сильный стимулятор!
examples.trans: Everything is clear, this is definitely a strong stimulant!

examples.text: Сильный ищет способ, а слабый ищет причину.

examples.text: На улице дул сильный ветер.
examples.trans: A strong wind was blowing outside.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'stimulant', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Всё понятно, это точно сильный стимулятор!

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (root 'мешивать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to powder'.

examples.text: Они подмешивают порошок прямо в курицу!
examples.trans: They are mixing the powder right into the chicken!

examples.text: Подождите, это что, настоящая жидкая курица?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'powder', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Вчера вечером я оставляла здесь редкие порошки.
examples.trans: Last night I left rare powders here.

examples.text: Катя, я знаю, где твои странные порошки.
examples.trans: Katya, I know where your strange powders are.

examples.text: Послушайте меня, эти порошки абсолютно легальные!
examples.trans: Listen to me, these powders are completely legal!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.text: Я уже успел сходить утром в душ.
examples.trans: I already managed to take a shower in the morning.

examples.text: До встречи в нашем любимом ресторане!
examples.trans: See you at our beloved restaurant!

examples.text: Она приехала ко мне ненадолго в гости.
examples.trans: She came to visit me for a short while.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'comrade', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Товарищ лейтенант, это обычные пищевые добавки!

examples.text: Товарищ капитан, зачем вы его сейчас отпустили?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'captain', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('we') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: Вчера вечером у нас случилась большая оплошность.
examples.trans: Last night a big indiscretion happened between us.

examples.text: Вера Ивановна, извините, мы ужасно спешим!
examples.trans: Vera Ivanovna, excuse us, we are in a terrible hurry!

examples.text: Лёва, давай быстрее, нам пора на кухню!
examples.trans: Lyova, hurry up, it is time for us to go to the kitchen!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'now'.

examples.text: Так, задержанный гражданин, вы теперь полностью свободны!
examples.trans: All right, detained citizen, you are now completely free!

examples.text: Товарищ капитан, что мы теперь будем делать?
examples.trans: Comrade Captain, what are we going to do now?

examples.text: Теперь докладывайте по порядку, что вы делаете?
examples.trans: Now report in order, what are you doing here?

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to be'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: То, что было вчера, — просто случайность!
examples.trans: What happened yesterday was just a fluke!

examples.text: Случайность, а может быть, это наша судьба?
examples.trans: A fluke, or maybe it is our destiny?

examples.text: Честно говоря, я была лучшего мнения.
examples.trans: Honestly speaking, I had a better opinion of you.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to do', forming an aspectual pair with 'сделать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Скажи, а что ты вообще тут делаешь?
examples.trans: Tell me, what are you even doing here?

examples.text: И что вы обычно с этим порошком делаете?
examples.trans: And what do you usually do with this powder?

examples.text: Товарищ капитан, что мы теперь будем делать?
examples.trans: Comrade Captain, what are we going to do now?

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'immediately'.

вызывать.gloss: to cause, to raise; to call

meanings.en: to cause, to raise; to call
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (root 'зывать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to cause', forming an aspectual pair with 'вызвать'.

examples.text: Немедленно вызываем сюда нашу группу захвата!
examples.trans: We are immediately calling our arrest team here!

examples.text: Упаковка не вызывает подозрений.
examples.trans: The packaging doesn't raise suspicion.

examples.text: Я вызываю такси.
examples.trans: I'm calling a taxi.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'here'.

examples.text: А вот и серьёзные поставщики приехали сюда!

examples.text: Немедленно вызываем сюда нашу группу захвата!

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вчера говорил напиток, а сейчас говорит начальник!

examples.trans: Oh, this is my beloved niece who arrived!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (root 'казать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to show', forming an aspectual pair with 'показывать'.

examples.text: Откройте вашу сумку и покажите мне, пожалуйста.

examples.text: А сейчас мы покажем вам наш десерт!
examples.trans: And now we will show you our dessert!

examples.text: Покажите руки!
examples.trans: Show me your hands!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.
